31	// detailsShortcuts is the detail's column: the same six keys for every finding,
32	// each greyed when it has nothing to act on (Rule 130). Every availability is
33	// computed from the finding on screen alone, so the header reads no file. The
34	// descriptions are at most ten cells: the column is 19 cells wide at 80 columns
35	// and `<ctrl+o>` takes nine of them.
36	func (m Model) detailsShortcuts() shortcut.Shortcuts {
37		// A finding with no published reference is the same screen as one with three,
38		// so W is greyed rather than dropped. keymap.Web is what handleDetailsState
39		// binds: a key advertised under another name would do nothing.
40		f := m.selectedFinding
41		return []shortcut.Shortcut{
42			{Key: "esc", Description: "Back"},
43			{Key: keymap.Web, Description: "Open ref", Disabled: f == nil || len(f.References) == 0},
44			{Key: "enter", Description: "Open file", Disabled: !m.canOpenFindingFile().Enabled()},
45			{Key: writeRemediationKey, Description: "Apply fix", Disabled: !m.canFixMisconfig().Enabled()},
46			{Key: keymap.Copy, Description: "Copy cmd", Disabled: !m.canCopyFixCommand().Enabled()},
47			{Key: keymap.Exclude, Description: "Exclude", Disabled: !m.canExclude().Enabled()},
48		}
49	}

51	// resultsShortcuts advertises the findings table's own keys.
52	//
53	// The four severity toggles were bound and unadvertised — a user had to open
54	// the help to learn the view filtered at all — and `.` was offered on three
55	// tabs out of four, from back when it cycled the severity floor. It is the sort
56	// now (Rule 111), so it applies wherever there is a table.
57	//
58	// While the search has the keyboard, everything else is a character: listing
59	// keys that no longer do what they say is worse than listing nothing, so only
60	// the two that end the search are shown. Same shape as the ports view.
61	func (m Model) resultsShortcuts() shortcut.Shortcuts {
62		if m.findingsTable.InEditMode() {
63			return shortcut.Shortcuts{{Key: "enter/esc", Description: "Confirm / Cancel search"}}
64		}
65		// X is greyed rather than dropped (Rule 130): a tab is not a different
66		// screen, and the entry used to appear and disappear as the cursor crossed
67		// a Trivy secret in a list holding both tools' findings.
68		// The Remediation tab has a table of its own: what filters and sorts the
69		// findings does not reach it, so those keys are greyed there and S — which
70		// means nothing on the four tabs of findings — is the one that lights up.
71		notFindings := m.activeTab == TabRemediation
72		// Enter opens the selected finding, or on the Remediation tab the diff of the
73		// chosen bases: one key, the same place in the column, a different verb.
74		enter := shortcut.Shortcut{Key: "enter", Description: "Details", Disabled: !m.canOpenFinding().Enabled()}
75		if m.isGrouped() {
76			enter = shortcut.Shortcut{Key: "enter", Description: "Open group", Disabled: !m.canOpenGroup().Enabled()}
77		}
78		if notFindings {
79			enter = shortcut.Shortcut{Key: "enter", Description: "Show diff", Disabled: !m.canPreviewRemediation().Enabled()}
80		}
81		// ctrl+o is one key with one verb — write the file — and the object it
82		// writes is the tab's. The label changes with it so the column never
83		// offers "Write Dockerfile" on a tab holding a Kubernetes manifest.
84		writeShortcut := shortcut.Shortcut{Key: writeRemediationKey, Description: "Write Dockerfile", Disabled: !m.canWriteRemediation().Enabled()}
85		if m.activeTab == TabMisconfig {
86			writeShortcut = shortcut.Shortcut{Key: writeRemediationKey, Description: "Apply built-in fix", Disabled: !m.canFixMisconfig().Enabled()}
87		}
88		return []shortcut.Shortcut{
89			{Key: "tab", Description: "Switch tab"},
90			enter,
91			// Third, so that it is among the seven entries that show at 80 columns.
92			{Key: groupToggleKey, Description: m.groupToggleLabel(), Disabled: !m.canGroup().Enabled()},
93			{Key: "space", Description: "Choose candidate", Disabled: !m.canSelectCandidate().Enabled()},
94			writeShortcut,

96			{Key: "c", Description: "Toggle CRITICAL", Disabled: notFindings},

132		base := theme.IconSecurity + " Security Scanner"

134			return base + " " + theme.IconChevronRight + " Inventory"

156	// GetHeaderInfo returns the key-value info for the header: the context, one
157	// count, and in the results how much of it is fixable.
158	//
159	// It used to carry seven fields in the results state, which is exactly the
160	// number buildInfoLines renders — an eighth would have been dropped in silence.
161	// Most of them had stopped earning their line:
162	//
163	//   - Trivy and Gitleaks versions answered "can I scan?", which the dashboard
164	//     already answers from shared.State.Tools, and which an inventory of past
165	//     scans is not about.
166	//   - Filter showed the severity filter, permanently reading ALL, and meaning
167	//     nothing on the Secrets tab or in the details.
168	//   - Secrets and Licenses duplicated the tab bar, which renders the same two
169	//     numbers a line below.
170	//
171	// Fixable came back on its own merits: it is the one figure that says what can
172	// be done, which none of the removed ones did.
173	//
174	// The context is what replaced them, and it is the one thing that was missing:
175	// the scan caches are scoped to a context, so the same inventory rows mean
176	// different things in two of them and look identical.
177	func (m Model) GetHeaderInfo(context string) []shortcut.HeaderInfo {
178		info := []shortcut.HeaderInfo{
179			{Key: "Context", Value: context, Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle},
180		}
181		if key, value, ok := m.headerCount(); ok {
182			info = append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: key, Value: value, Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle})
183		}
184		if mode, ok := m.groupModeHeader(); ok {
185			info = append(info, mode)
186		}
187		if pss, ok := m.pssHeader(); ok {
188			info = append(info, pss)
189		}
190		if value, style, ok := m.headerFixable(); ok {
191			info = append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: "Fixable", Value: value, Style: style})
192		}
193		if value, ok := m.headerUnrendered(); ok {
194			info = append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: "Not rendered", Value: value, Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle})
195		}
196		if sig, ok := m.signatureHeader(); ok {
197			info = append(info, sig)
198		}
199		return info
200	}
201	
202	// groupModeHeader names the grouped display in the info column, whole where the
203	// column has room for it. The shortcut column says the way back; this says where
204	// the user is.
205	func (m Model) groupModeHeader() (shortcut.HeaderInfo, bool) {
206		if m.state != StateResults || !m.isGrouped() {
207			return shortcut.HeaderInfo{}, false
208		}
209		return shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: "View", Value: labelGroupByFix, Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle}, true
210	}
211	
212	// headerUnrendered is how many Helm charts and Kustomize overlays the schema
213	// stage could not look at, for want of helm or kustomize (§3.80). Without it a
214	// repository of charts would read as schema-clean when nothing was checked.
215	// Absent when there are none — it is not a count of findings, and a "0" on
216	// every result would be noise about a stage most repositories do not need.
217	func (m Model) headerUnrendered() (string, bool) {
218		if !m.showsResult() || m.result == nil || len(m.result.K8sUnrendered) == 0 {
219			return "", false
220		}
221		return strconv.Itoa(len(m.result.K8sUnrendered)) + " (install helm / kustomize)", true
222	}

224	// headerFixable is how many of the vulnerabilities have a fixed version, split
225	// by what has to move: "12 (8 base, 4 deps)". It is the one number that says
226	// what can be done about the findings, which the count above does not. Like the
227	// count, it is absent where the state is a list of nothing, and it is present
228	// on both sides of the results/details step so the header does not change
229	// under the reader (Rule 130).
230	func (m Model) headerFixable() (string, lipgloss.Style, bool) {
231		if !m.showsResult() || m.result == nil {
232			return "", lipgloss.Style{}, false
233		}
234		s := remediation.Summarize(m.result.Findings)
235		if s.Fixable() == 0 {
236			return "0", theme.DimStyle, true
237		}
238		var parts []string
239		if s.BaseImage > 0 {
240			parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(s.BaseImage)+" base")
241		}
242		if s.Dependencies > 0 {
243			parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(s.Dependencies)+" deps")
244		}
245		if s.Unclassified > 0 {
246			parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(s.Unclassified)+" unclassified")
247		}
248		return strconv.Itoa(s.Fixable()) + " (" + strings.Join(parts, ", ") + ")", theme.HeaderValueStyle, true
249	}

content.content:
- *Links are looked at twice.* `staysInside` refuses a path or a root that does not resolve for any reason other than
  "does not exist" (a loop of links, a permission), where it used to let it through. The write Cmd of `ctrl+o` calls it
  again right before `patch.WriteIfUnchanged` (`errLeavesTarget`, footer `Nothing was written to <file> — ...`): a link
  put in place between the confirmation and the write, to a file holding the same bytes, passes the content check and
  would have been written through. A small window remains between that check and the write itself.
- *Names and logs.* A file name comes from the repository: `shownName` (`withoutControlSpace`, on one line) is applied to
  it in the confirmation and in the footers of the write and the verdict. Logs carry the relative path and the cause
  only (`withoutPath` drops the operation and the absolute path of a `PathError` or `LinkError`).

### Group by fix — `g` on the CVE tab (DEVDESK-754)

A scan of an image lists the same cause many times: three CVEs of one package are one move. `g` on the CVE tab
swaps the body of the results from the findings table to **one row per cause**, and back. It is a display toggle
(a lowercase letter, declared in `keymap.localToggles` for `security/findings`), not a seventh tab: the tab bar
keeps its six tabs.

**The model.** `remediation.GroupAll` (pure, see "What can be fixed") returns one `Fix` per package and installed
version, fixed or not, with its `Members`; `cveGroups` (`fixgroup.go`) turns them into `fixGroup` rows: severity
(the worst of the members), `Subject` (the package, or the ID of a vulnerability that names no package),
`Change` (`1.1.1k -> 1.1.1w`; `1.2 -> abc or def` when the versions could not be ordered; `1.2 -> none`),
`Target`, `Status` (the closed vocabulary of `fixStatusOf`: `Manual` for a fixable CVE, `No fix published`
otherwise), `Command` and `Members`. `Command` is the `Fix.Command` only when `scan.PlainWords` accepts it, the
same gate as the detail's `Run` line: a group with a command that is not plain words has none, and `Y` says so.
The key of a group (`groupKey`: ecosystem, package, installed version, unfixed, position) is what a re-scan finds the
row again by. A vulnerability with no package is its own group (assumption: a CVE with no package name is its own
cause); `Fix.Position` (0 for a named package, else 1, 2, ... among the bare vulnerabilities of one ID, ecosystem and
version) keeps two of them, or one and a package named like its ID, from sharing a key. The scan's text shown in a
group (package, versions, candidates) goes through `inlineText` (`withoutControlSpace` on one line) when `cveGroups`
builds the row, so the title, the footer sentence and the cells carry no escape sequence, control or bidi mark. Rows are ordered by worst severity, then number of CVEs, then package, then change.

**Fixable and the groups.** The header's `Fixable` is still `remediation.Summarize(...).Fixable()`, grouped or
not. The CVEs of the groups that are not `Unfixed` add up to it, and the CVEs of the `Unfixed` groups (`No fix
published`) to its `Unfixed` count: a group nobody can fix is said in words and never counted as fixable. Nothing
is ever marked done: a `fixGroup` has no such field, and a row shrinks or goes away only because a re-scan says
so.

**One table in the place of another.** `Model.groups` is a second `datatable.Model[fixGroup]` (`cveGroupColumns`:
Severity, Package, Change, CVEs, Fix, each with its `Sizing`; cells are plain text, only Severity is coloured and
it is also its word). `renderResultsView` returns `m.groups.View()` while `isGrouped()`, so the body is a table
with a header whatever it holds (Rule 139). The findings table is never touched by the switch (`updateFindingsTable`,
which calls `GotoTop`, is not called): its severity tokens, search query, sort and cursor are what the user left.
Severity tokens, the search (`/`), the tabs and `p` keep driving the findings table; the groups listed are the ones
with **at least one member the findings table shows** (`visibleGroups`), and each row's count is the whole group,
hidden members included, since one move closes them all. `.` and the cursor keys drive the groups table.
`refreshGroups` runs after every change of what the findings table shows (a token, the search typed or pasted, a tab switch, a
result) and keeps the cursor on its group by key, else at the nearest index.

**Going in and out.** In, the cursor is on the group of the selected finding (`groupIndexOf`). Out, the findings
cursor goes to the first visible member of the group under the cursor, else the finding that was selected, else the
same position (`nearestFinding`). The mode is `groupedTabs [tabCount]bool`, held per tab for the life of the view:
it survives a tab switch and reopening a result from the inventory. Only the CVE tab groups until SC2
(Misconfigurations): elsewhere `g` is greyed with `Group by fix covers the CVE tab`, and with `No vulnerability to
group` on a CVE tab with no CVE. In the grouped list it is never greyed, since it is the way back.

**The group level (`StateGroup`).** `enter` on a group opens a level of its own: the group's findings
(`groupTable`, the findings' columns minus File), all of them, filtered out or not. Four keys: `esc` Back, `enter`
Details, `Y` Copy cmd, `?` Help. `enter` there opens the same finding detail as from the flat table through
`openDetail(f, parent)`, which every way in uses and which sets `detailsParent`; `esc` in the detail, and
`refreshDetails` when a re-scan clears the finding, go back to `detailsParent` (the group, or the results). Tabs,
filters, the sort and the other actions do nothing one level down. The title names the group
(`Security Scanner (target) › openssl 1.1.1k -> 1.1.1w`); the header keeps its figures and in the grouped list also
says `View: Group by fix`.

**Keys.** `g` is the third entry of the results column (so it is among the seven that show at 80 columns, and `h`
moves out of them); its word is `Group by fix`, `List by finding` once on. `Y` is in the column on every tab, greyed
with `Copy the command from a group (g), or from a finding's detail` in the flat list. In the grouped list and the
group level it copies the group's command (`apk upgrade openssl`, `go get ...`) through `writeClipboard`, whole, from
the Cmd (Rule 110), as the detail's `Y` does: DevDesk never runs it (`never_run_guard_test.go` covers the new
function: `copyGroupCommand` is a root of the copy path and `.Command` on a group or a `remediation.Fix` counts as reading the command). It is greyed `No fix is published for this group` for an unfixed
group, `This group has no command to run` for one with several candidate versions or a command that is not plain
words. `space`, `ctrl+o` and `S` act on one finding, so in the grouped list they are greyed and say `Open the group
to act on one finding`. The footer says what the selected group does, derived on every frame: `3 CVEs closed by one
move to 1.1.1w`, `No fix published for 2 CVEs`, or the count and the candidate versions when none is preferred; a
failed stage's error takes precedence.

**A re-scan is the only truth (AC5, AC7).** `setResult` (what a verification re-scan hands back) rebuilds the groups
from the new result (`groupsFollowResult`), then the group level by key (`refreshGroupLevel`: members read again, the
cursor kept on the finding the user was on; a group that is gone steps back to the grouped list), then the detail
(`refreshDetails`, which returns to the group or to the results). A result opened from the inventory starts with no
group level but keeps the mode.

**Limits.** The tab bar (`CVE (n)  Secrets (n) ...`) is wider than 80 columns as soon as counts have two digits,
grouped or not; that is a separate bug and is not fixed here, so the width tests measure the table, the filter bar,
the info line and the header, not the tab bar. `sameFinding` ignores the line, so two instances with the same
title and message in one file are one identity for the selection (the nearest finding may be the first of them).
The group's `Fix` word comes from `fixStatusOf`, the detail's from `m.fixStatus`, which also knows a stale preview:

content.content:
The group's `Fix` word comes from `fixStatusOf`, the detail's from `m.fixStatus`, which also knows a stale preview:
a group may say `Built-in fix available` while its detail says unavailable. The Misconfigurations tab (File and rule
groups) is SC2.

### The Pod Security profile of a finding (DEVDESK-686)

Trivy anchors the Kubernetes rules that implement the Pod Security Standards
(PSS) to a profile: the first `References` entry that points at
`kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/` ends in
`#baseline` or `#restricted`. DevDesk shows that profile on every such finding
and lets the user hide, on the Misconfigurations tab, what the profile it aims at
does not require. It labels and filters; it fixes nothing, and Trivy stays the
only source of findings.

**The table.** `internal/remediation/pss.go` holds `pssProfiles`, a map from
`RuleKey` to `Profile`, written by hand. `PodSecurity(finding)` returns the
profile and whether the finding is a Pod Security one. It answers `false` for
anything that is not a Trivy misconfiguration (`Source` is not
`SourceTrivyMisconfig`), so kubeconform and build-context findings never get a
profile.
